mappings.X3: oriented to person, time and place

g_rules.rule: Use the most detailed (most specific child) concept that is fully entailed by the span. All components of the chosen concept must be supported by the text; do not infer details beyond what is written.

Only assign the most detailed concept when ALL of its components are fully entailed by the text. If a modifier (e.g. 'chronic') is textually separate and not clearly linked to the finding, annotate the components separately rather than combining them into one pre-coordinated concept.
Where a single suitable pre-coordinated concept exists for a span, use it. Do not split a span into multiple separate concepts if one concept captures the full meaning.

Prefer multiple concepts over a single concept only when the multiple concepts extract greater clinical detail than the single concept alone. For example, if a single concept loses body-site specificity, use two concepts (body structure + procedure) instead.
If no pre-coordinated concept exists for a complex clinical phrase, decompose it into a compound of concepts (e.g. Procedure + Morphological Abnormality + Body Structure).
Annotation spans must not be discontinuous or overlapping. If two concepts would overlap textually, choose non-overlapping spans and assign the most appropriate concept to each.

Apply the +/- 1 sentence contextual proximity rule: when considering which context to use for making an annotation more specific, look only at the previous sentence, current sentence, and next sentence. Ignore contextual information from further away in the note.

Check for homonyms that may be incorrectly associated with a clinical concept. Only annotate a word when it is used in its clinical/medical sense, not when the same word appears in a non-clinical context.
Where a finding is explicitly negated and a specific SNOMED CT negative/absent concept exists (e.g. 'apyrexial' for 'no fever'), use that specific negative concept.

Unverified, self-reported, or explicitly negated findings should still be annotated with the positive concept when no specific negative SNOMED CT concept exists. The task is entity detection, not assertion classification.

Do not annotate incidental mentions of clinical terms that are not referencing the concept itself. For example, 'married to an epilepsy nurse' should not produce an epilepsy annotation because the disorder is not being referenced in a clinical context.

Annotate concepts that are present in the text through misspellings, non-standard abbreviations, or synonyms. Map these to the correct SNOMED CT concept regardless of the surface form used in the text.
When a term exists in multiple SNOMED hierarchies, use context to determine the correct hierarchy. If context is insufficient, apply this priority: Procedure > Finding > Body Structure.

Ignore structured section headings in MIMIC-IV discharge notes (e.g. 'Allergies:', 'Chief Complaint:', 'History of Present Illness:', 'Past Medical History:', 'Social History:', 'Family History:', 'Physical Exam:', 'Pertinent Results:', 'Brief Hospital Course:', 'Medications on Admission:', 'Discharge Medications:', 'Discharge Disposition:', 'Discharge Diagnosis:', 'Discharge Condition:', 'Discharge Instructions:', 'Followup Instructions:'). Do not annotate these headings.

Since physical objects are out of scope, use the 'in situ' finding concept for devices that are present/in place, and use the corresponding procedure concept when the text describes insertion or removal of the device.
Ignore lab result sections ('LABS ON ADMISSION', 'LABS ON DISCHARGE') as these contain heavily redacted data requiring specialist knowledge to interpret.
Time-boxing: if uncertain whether to include or exclude an annotation after reasonable consideration, exclude it. If uncertain whether to use a child or parent concept, use the parent.
When a body structure span is ambiguous between the entire structure and a part of the structure, prefer the parent concept 'Structure of ...' rather than a more specific sub-structure.

Only use SNOMED CT concepts from the following top-level hierarchies: Findings, Body Structures, Situation with Explicit Context, and Procedures. Concepts from other hierarchies (e.g. physical object, substance, product) are out of scope.

stage_1_span.label: Detailed_Span
stage_1_span.description: A text span whose surrounding context may support a more specific concept than the literal words alone

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search for the most specific concept whose ENTIRE meaning is entailed by the text. Consider modifiers and qualifiers appearing in the same or adjacent sentences (+/- 1 sentence)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select the most detailed concept only if ALL components are fully supported by the text. If any component is not entailed, fall back to the parent concept or decompose into separate annotations

stage_1_span.label: Complex_Phrase
stage_1_span.description: A clinical phrase that could be represented as a single pre-coordinated concept or as multiple post-coordinated concepts

stage_2_search.intent_translation: First search for a single pre-coordinated concept. If one exists, use it. If multiple concepts would capture greater detail (e.g. body-site specificity), search for the component concepts as well

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Prefer a single pre-coordinated concept unless decomposition into multiple concepts captures clinically significant additional detail. If no pre-coordinated concept exists, use a compound of Procedure + Morphologic Abnormality + Body Structure as needed

stage_1_span.label: Negated_Finding
stage_1_span.description: A clinical finding that is explicitly negated, denied, or noted as absent

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search for both the positive form and the negative/absent SNOMED CT concept for the finding (e.g. 'apyrexial' for absent fever, 'no family history of ...' for specific situation concepts)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: If a specific SNOMED CT negative/absent concept exists, use it. Otherwise, annotate with the positive finding concept. Never skip annotation merely because a finding is negated or unconfirmed

stage_1_span.label: Incidental_Term
stage_1_span.description: A term that lexically matches a clinical concept but is used in a non-clinical or incidental context

stage_2_search.filtering_logic: Drop the annotation entirely if the term is used in a non-clinical context (e.g. as part of a job title, metaphor, or non-medical reference)
stage_2_search.intent_translation: Do not search; this span should not be annotated

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Reject annotation. Incidental mentions should produce no annotation to teach algorithms about irrelevant contexts

stage_1_span.label: Non_Standard_Term
stage_1_span.description: A misspelled clinical term, non-standard abbreviation, or clinical synonym that should still be annotated

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Correct the misspelling or expand the abbreviation to the standard medical term, then search for the corresponding SNOMED concept

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select the concept matching the intended clinical meaning, not the literal surface form

stage_1_span.label: Ambiguous_Hierarchy
stage_1_span.description: A clinical term that appears in multiple SNOMED CT hierarchies (e.g. Finding vs Body Structure, Procedure vs Finding)

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search across all applicable hierarchies and use clinical context to determine the correct one

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Use context to select the correct hierarchy. If context is insufficient: Procedure > Finding > Body Structure. For diagnosed conditions, prefer disorder (child of finding). For excised/removed structures, prefer morphologic abnormality

stage_1_span.label: Section_Heading
stage_1_span.description: A structured MIMIC-IV section heading such as 'Allergies:', 'Chief Complaint:', 'Physical Exam:', etc.

stage_2_search.filtering_logic: Drop entirely. Section headings are not annotated
stage_2_search.intent_translation: Do not search; section headings should not produce annotations

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Reject annotation. Structured headings in discharge notes are excluded from annotation

stage_1_span.label: Device_Reference
stage_1_span.description: A reference to a physical device (catheter, tube, line, drain, stent, etc.) in clinical text

stage_2_search.intent_translation: If the device is described as being present/in place, search for the 'in situ' finding concept. If the text describes insertion or removal, search for the corresponding procedure concept

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Never select physical object hierarchy concepts. For devices in place: select the 'in situ' finding. For insertion/removal: select the procedure concept

stage_1_span.label: Lab_Result
stage_1_span.description: Content appearing under LABS ON ADMISSION or LABS ON DISCHARGE sections

stage_2_search.filtering_logic: Drop entirely. Lab result sections are excluded from annotation
stage_2_search.intent_translation: Do not search; lab results in admission/discharge sections should not be annotated

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Reject annotation. Lab result sections require specialist interpretation and are out of scope

stage_1_span.label: Context_Dependent
stage_1_span.description: A span whose annotation specificity depends on contextual information from nearby sentences

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Include contextual information from the previous, current, and next sentence to make the search more specific (e.g. a nearby body site reference can qualify a procedure or finding)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Only use context from +/- 1 sentence to increase specificity. If context from further away would change the concept, ignore it and use the less specific concept

stage_1_span.label: Homonym
stage_1_span.description: A word that has both clinical and non-clinical meanings depending on context (e.g. 'fit' as seizure vs. 'fit' as exercise)

stage_2_search.filtering_logic: Only proceed with search if the word is used in its clinical/medical sense
stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search for the clinical concept only when the surrounding context confirms medical usage

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select the concept only for the clinical usage instance. Mark non-clinical usage instances as incorrect/excluded

stage_1_span.label: Any_Concept
stage_1_span.description: Any candidate annotation that may resolve to an out-of-scope SNOMED hierarchy

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Restrict search to the four in-scope hierarchies: Findings, Body Structures, Situation with Explicit Context, and Procedures

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Reject any candidate concept not in the four allowed top-level hierarchies. Never select concepts from Physical Object, Substance, Product, Qualifier Value, or other out-of-scope hierarchies

stage_1_span.label: Body_Structure
stage_1_span.description: A reference to a body structure where it is unclear whether the entire structure or a sub-part is meant

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search for both the specific sub-structure and the parent 'Structure of ...' concept

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: If it is not clear whether the span refers to the entire structure or a sub-part, prefer the parent concept 'Structure of ...' over a more specific sub-structure

_source_meta.note: Rules derived from the official SNOMED CT Entity Linking annotation guidelines. The annotation_rule_map is empty because these rules are guideline-derived rather than annotation-specific.
